cases.knownIssue: Lost the `ambiguousKind` flag in the preset swap. `BluReceiptParser` INFERRED a transfer from a bank name sitting beside an account number and flagged its own inference; a pattern matches the literal 'Admin Fee' and types it `.transfer`, which is a stated fact and correctly carries no flag. The row is identical in every other respect — amount, merchant, kind and subtype all match. cases.name: unknown-sender-is-never-fetched
cases.note: A real receipt from a sender nothing knows. It is not skipped — it is never requested: GmailRail narrows its query to from:(the domains of parsers it already has), so an unknown sender's mail never arrives to be judged. Harmless for capture, fatal for discovery: PatternDiscovery can only propose patterns for senders the app can already read. Feeding it live mail needs a fetch that is not scoped to known parsers.

cases.name: learned-pattern-refund
cases.note: A refund read by a LEARNED pattern rather than a hand-written parser. Before markers carried a type this could only ever come out as `nonSpend` with no subtype, or — if the model proposed no marker at all — as spending, which adds a reversal to the total it reverses. It also PAIRS with `learned-pattern-purchase`: same merchant, same amount, a day later, so it carries `reversal` naming the charge it undoes. Flagged, never netted — the refund stays non-spend and the purchase stays spend, and the person decides what the pair means. No `ambiguousKind`: 'Refund Processed' is the sender's own words.

discovery.note: Selection only — no model, so this asserts WHICH senders and how many layouts the loop would spend calls on, never what the model would say. Nothing here is readable by any parser, and that is the point: an OOV sender failing to parse is the gap the agentic loop exists to close. What must work is that the loop SEES it. swiftpay is deliberately awkward — two subjects, two layouts, the amount labelled Nominal in half the payments and Jumlah in the other half, merchants ending at two different terminators, and every third figure written with no Rp prefix at all.

expectedNonCandidates.deals.example.com: templated and full of Rp, but every email quotes the same three prices — a brochure, refused on amount variance
expectedNonCandidates.tinyshop.example.com: genuine receipts, only three of them — below the evidence floor, so it waits rather than guessing
expectedNonCandidates.northwind.example.com: no Rp or IDR anywhere, so the currency filter drops it before selection
expectedNonCandidates.blubybcadigital.id: already readable — its mail is not unread
expectedNonCandidates.grab.com: already readable by two learned patterns
expectedNonCandidates.zenpay.example.com: already readable by a learned pattern — the one that carries typed non-spend markers

layoutKnownIssues.swiftpay.co.id: Two subjects, and the subject pass keeps only the dominant one, so the 8 'Top Up Berhasil' emails are discarded before body clustering runs. Expected 1 layout where the sender really has 2. blu loses a third layout of 12 real receipts the same way.
